name: OpenBao
summary: An open-source secret-management service that protects an untrusted storage backend behind a barrier, routes policy-authorized requests to mounted engines, and manages expiring credentials.

features.name: Barrier-encrypted storage
features.description: OpenBao encrypts data before sending it to a durable storage backend treated as untrusted, then loads audit devices, auth methods, and secrets engines after unseal.
benefits: Separates durable storage from plaintext secret access
Allows supported storage backends to share one protected service model
costs: Unseal and key-management state gates availability
Encryption and storage failures are coupled to service recovery

features.name: Policy-authorized mounted-engine routing
features.description: OpenBao authenticates clients, resolves policies, and routes authorized requests to mounted secrets engines while emitting request and response events to configured audit devices.
benefits: Composes authentication, ACL policy, and engine implementations behind a common core
Makes secret-engine placement and policy scope explicit
costs: Policy, mount, and audit configuration must remain consistent
A request path crosses security and backend routing boundaries

features.name: Lease-based expiration and revocation
features.description: OpenBao attaches lease identities to leased secrets and tokens, permits renewal or revocation, and automatically revokes a secret when its lease expires.
benefits: Makes revocation a first-class lifecycle operation
costs: Clients must renew before expiry or recover from revocation
Expiration management introduces timing and background-work state

mathematical_views.model: Barrier and seal operational state machine
mathematical_views.question: How do sealed, unsealed, and post-unseal states constrain access to protected state and mounted services?
assumptions: The encryption key cannot be recovered while sealed
The configured unseal procedure establishes the unsealed transition

mathematical_views.question: How does a client request flow from authentication through policy evaluation, engine routing, lease registration, and audit emission?
assumptions: Policies determine allowed actions on paths
Mounted engines implement the selected operation
Audit delivery is modeled as an observation edge rather than a request precondition

mathematical_views.question: Which transitions preserve a credential's validity, renew it, revoke it, or move it to an expired state?
assumptions: Lease duration and renewal rules are authoritative
Revocation is applied according to engine and token-store contracts
Clock and scheduler behavior are abstracted

benefits: Protects persisted state across storage backends
costs: Key custody and unseal operations become availability dependencies

benefits: Extensible secret and auth engine composition
costs: Routing and ACL configuration require careful lifecycle management

benefits: Bounded credential lifetime and explicit revocation
costs: Renewal and expiration handling adds application complexity
